text:
Brock Boeser is having the season Vancouver has waited years for, and it has landed him in trade chat anyway. The Province ran "Canucks Live: Bargain bin shopping as Brock Boeser enters trade chat," while Canucks Army asked whether a "suddenly surging Brock Boeser" is now on a value contract.

The surge is real on the scoresheet: 28 points in 27 games, 18 of them on the power play, with Elias Pettersson hurt and more of the offense running through him. He's playing over 21 minutes a night lately and set up both of Marco Rossi's goals in a three-assist night against Minnesota.

Our numbers urge caution at even strength. Vancouver gets only 36% of the expected goals (chance quality) at five on five with Boeser on, worse than without him, and his teammates have finished 4.8 goals above what those chances deserve. His points pace is well above our talent range of 2.02 to 2.72 per 60. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, with chances against piling up when he's on.

That's the tension for the Canucks: a power-play producer at peak value, on a team that lost seven of its last ten.
headline: Boeser's career year, and the trade talk
